title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
貴州鄉試錄序
今
上龍飛四年爲萬曆丙子兩畿十
三省復當秋試在貴州則巡
按御史秦時吉寔監臨之先
期走幣四方聘諸文學旣至
則以登龍暨敎諭陳光宇爲
===
考試官敎諭謝蘇王汝爲蘄
邪僎爲同考試官提調則屬
之左布政使李心學左叅政
林澄源監試則屬之按察使
林梴章副使王天爵餘百執
事咸愼簡以充八月丙寅會
於舉院御史曰爲
punctuated:
貴州鄉試錄序
今上龍飛四年，爲萬曆丙子，兩畿十三省復當秋試。在貴州，則巡按御史秦時吉寔監臨之。先期，走幣四方，聘諸文學。旣至，則以登龍暨敎諭陳光宇爲考試官；敎諭謝蘇、王汝爲、蘄邪僎爲同考試官。提調則屬之左布政使李心學、左叅政林澄源；監試則屬之按察使林梴章、副使王天爵；餘百執事咸愼簡以充。八月丙寅，會於舉院。御史曰：「爲
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guizhou Provincial Examination

In the fourth year since the reigning Emperor ascended the throne, which is the bingzi year of the Wanli era [1576], the two Metropolitan Areas and thirteen Provinces were once again due to hold the autumn examinations. In Guizhou, Regional Inspector Qin Shiji 秦時吉 served as Supervising Official. Prior to the scheduled date, he dispatched gifts in all directions to invite various men of letters. Once they had arrived, he appointed me, [first name] Denglong 登龍, together with Instructor Chen Guangyu 陳光宇 as Examiners; and Instructors Xie Su 謝蘇, Wang Ruwei 王汝爲, and Qi Xieshuan 蘄邪僎 [?] as Associate Examiners. The duties of Proctor were assigned to Left Administration Commissioner Li Xinxue 李心學 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Lin Chengyuan 林澄源; the duties of Surveillance Official were assigned to Surveillance Commissioner Lin Yanzhang 林梴章 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Tianjue 王天爵; and all the remaining hundred functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts. title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
國求賢允惟
鉅典小大外内宜罔弗欽持衡惟
平秉鑑惟明諸文學事也慎
之哉章程必備矩矱必飭藩
臬及百執事事也慎之哉既
肅戒而身率之羣工各敬官
執度越三日巳巳合提學副
使鄭旻所選士九百有奇試
之壬申再試乙亥三試遵
===
制額拔其尤者三十人幷梓其
文之優者二十篇爲錄以
獻
登龍當敷言於首簡乃言曰於
□
乎多士誕茲遡土荷被
聖祖
punctuated:
國求賢，允惟鉅典，小大外内，宜罔弗欽。持衡惟平，秉鑑惟明，諸文學事也，慎之哉！章程必備，矩矱必飭，藩臬及百執事事也，慎之哉！」既肅戒而身率之，羣工各敬官執度。越三日巳巳，合提學副使鄭旻所選士九百有奇試之。壬申再試，乙亥三試，遵制額拔其尤者三十人，幷梓其文之優者二十篇，爲錄以獻。
登龍當敷言於首簡，乃言曰：於□乎！多士誕茲遡土，荷被聖祖
translation_en:
… seeking worthies for the state is truly a grand institutional rite; all officials, whether great or small, inside or outside the examination compound, ought without exception to be reverent. Holding the balance with fairness and wielding the mirror with clarity—this is the duty of you instructors; be careful in it! Ensuring that the regulations are complete and the standards strictly enforced—this is the duty of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions and all the functionaries; be careful in it!” Having solemnly admonished them and led them in person, all the officials respectfully attended to their posts and upheld the rules. Three days later, on the jisi day, the more than nine hundred scholars selected by Education Intendant Vice Commissioner Zheng Min 鄭旻 were assembled and examined. On the renshen day they were examined a second time, and on the yihai day a third time. In accordance with the statutory quota, the thirty most outstanding candidates were selected, and twenty superior essays from among their compositions were printed to compile this record for presentation to the throne.
It falls to me, [Li] Denglong, to set forth a preface on the opening pages, and I say: Alas [?]! You many scholars, born in this remote land [?], have been graced by the Sacred Progenitor…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
神宗屢世熙洽之仁
明天子四載維新之化自蒿萊中
頡脫而出列於鄉書得上春
官冀待對於
大庭無論收與不收行皆有一
命之寄迨今伊始稱
帝臣矣其何以仰答
===
鴻造以明事
君之義而盡爲臣之責乎於乎多
士爾固皆以明經進者也易
首乾坤尊卑定矣含章從事
貴於有終有終者不二心之
謂也明乎不二心之義可以
爲臣矣股肱耳目書則況之
punctuated: 神宗屢世熙洽之仁、明天子四載維新之化，自蒿萊中頡脫而出，列於鄉書，得上春官，冀待對於大庭。無論收與不收，行皆有一命之寄，迨今伊始稱帝臣矣。其何以仰答鴻造，以明事君之義，而盡爲臣之責乎？於乎多士！爾固皆以明經進者也。《易》首《乾》、《坤》，尊卑定矣。含章從事，貴於有終。有終者，不二心之謂也。明乎不二心之義，可以爲臣矣。股肱耳目，《書》則況之，
translation_en:
…and the Divine Ancestors through generations of harmonious benevolence, as well as the renewing transformation of our Enlightened Son of Heaven over the past four years—have stood out and emerged from among the weeds of obscurity to be listed on the provincial examination register. You will now be able to advance to the Ministry of Rites, hoping to await the palace examination in the Great Court. Regardless of whether you are selected there or not, in time you will all be entrusted with an official appointment; beginning from today, you may already be called ministers of the Emperor. How, then, will you look up to repay this grand creation, clarify the principle of serving the Sovereign, and fulfill your responsibilities as ministers?

Alas, you many scholars! You have indeed all advanced through your mastery of the Classics. The Book of Changes (Yi) begins with the hexagrams Qian and Kun, whereby the positions of high and low are settled. Holding inner excellence while engaging in the ruler's affairs, what is valued is bringing things to completion. "Bringing things to completion" means having an undivided heart. Once you understand the principle of an undivided heart, you are fit to be a minister. As for limbs, eyes, and ears, the Book of Documents (Shu) uses them as a metaphor…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
以衛腹心以戴元首崇一體
也明乎一體之義可以爲臣
矣夙夜匪懈詩不云乎思皇
多士厥猶翼翼位之不懈民
之塈也民有攸塈然後足稱
靖共矣明乎靖共之義可以
爲臣矣春秋紀事王必稱天
===
覆冒之下何所逃乎宣猷勠
力皆其分也明乎無所逃之
義可以爲臣矣禮以表坊嚴
乎冠履服勤無隱是謂不欺
明乎不欺之義可以爲臣矣
於乎多士有司者固皆以爾
爲明經進者也念之哉爾尚
punctuated: 以衛腹心，以戴元首，崇一體也。明乎一體之義，可以爲臣矣。「夙夜匪懈」，《詩》不云乎？「思皇多士，厥猶翼翼。」位之不懈，民之塈也。民有攸塈，然後足稱靖共矣。明乎靖共之義，可以爲臣矣。《春秋》紀事，王必稱天。覆冒之下，何所逃乎？宣猷勠力，皆其分也。明乎無所逃之義，可以爲臣矣。《禮》以表坊，嚴乎冠履；服勤無隱，是謂不欺。明乎不欺之義，可以爲臣矣。於乎多士！有司者固皆以爾爲明經進者也，念之哉！爾尚
translation_en: …in order to guard the heart and belly and to support the head, honoring the principle of being a single body. Once one understands the principle of being a single body, one is fit to be a minister. “Never idle day or night”—does the Book of Odes (Shi) not say this? “How splendid are the many gentlemen; their counsels are reverent and careful.” Not being remiss in one's position brings rest to the people; only when the people have found rest can one truly be said to quietly fulfill one's duties. Once one understands the principle of quietly fulfilling one's duties, one is fit to be a minister. When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records events, the King is always styled “Heaven’s [King].” Beneath the canopy of Heaven, where can one escape? To set forth plans and exert one's strength in common effort are all one's proper duty. Once one understands the principle that there is nowhere to escape, one is fit to be a minister. The Book of Rites (Li) serves as a standard and a dike, strictly distinguishing cap from shoe; to labor in service while concealing nothing is what is called not deceiving. Once one understands the principle of not deceiving, one is fit to be a minister. Alas, you many gentlemen! The authorities have indeed selected you all as men advancing through mastery of the Classics. Bear this in mind! May you…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
思我
祖宗聖武神功闢爾封疆貽爾家
室囿爾庠序
皇上知臨顯比羅爾科目榮爾冠
紳寵爾祿位
恩私廣厚海嶽崇深勉効涓埃以
抒悃赤毋諉曰遐土之人未
===
易表見甘心自外有負
清時我聞曰玉韞山輝珠潛淵媚
蓋言籍也然崑岡合浦豈皆
近地哉人才之生亦何限於
地也封建之初何嘗貴筑亦
何嘗五嶺百粵卽八閩四蜀
皆稱裔土一有名世者出遂
punctuated: 思我祖宗聖武神功，闢爾封疆，貽爾家室，囿爾庠序；皇上知臨顯比，羅爾科目，榮爾冠紳，寵爾祿位。恩私廣厚，海嶽崇深，勉効涓埃，以抒悃赤。毋諉曰遐土之人，未易表見，甘心自外，有負清時。我聞曰：「玉韞山輝，珠潛淵媚。」蓋言籍也。然崑岡、合浦，豈皆近地哉？人才之生，亦何限於地也？封建之初，何嘗貴筑？亦何嘗五嶺、百粵？卽八閩、四蜀，皆稱裔土。一有名世者出，遂
translation_en: … reflect on how our Imperial Ancestors, with sacred martial valor and divine merit, opened up your borders, bequeathed to you your homes and families, and nurtured you in your schools; and how His Majesty, overseeing with wisdom and affiliating in openness, has gathered you through the examination system, honored you with official caps and sashes, and favored you with emoluments and rank. His grace and favor are vast and generous, as lofty as the mountains and as deep as the seas; strive to contribute even a drop of water or a speck of dust in order to express your sincere loyalty. Do not make excuses, saying that as men of a distant land it is not easy to distinguish yourselves, thus willingly excluding yourselves and failing this era of enlightened rule. I have heard it said: "When jade isenclosed in the mountain, the mountain shines; when pearls lie hidden in the deep, the abyss is charming." This speaks of what a place relies upon for its renown. Yet were Mount Kun and Hepu both nearby lands? How then could the birth of men of talent be restricted by geography? At the beginning of the feudal enfeoffments, what was Guizhu [Guizhou]? And what were the Five Ridges and the Hundred Yue? Even the Eight Min [Fujian] and the Four Shu [Sichuan] were all called remote borderlands. Yet once men of generational renown emerged from them, they…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
蔚爲文獻大邦由此言之果
人以地重抑地以人重耶考
之張九齡范鎮朱熹眞德秀
諸君子固閩蜀百粵之傑也
其所樹立表見微獨當時倚
之爲重歷今千百歲仰之曰
名臣曰眞儒尚聞風而興起
===
也朱子集諸儒之大成者爾
諸士資經術以靖獻類宗朱
子之說以探聖經之蘊觀其
言雖人人殊要皆闡道德之
奥而盡義理之極者也果能
言行合一終始不渝存之足
以修身而復性推之足以尊
punctuated: 蔚爲文獻大邦。由此言之，果人以地重，抑地以人重耶？考之張九齡、范鎮、朱熹、眞德秀諸君子，固閩、蜀、百粵之傑也。其所樹立表見，微獨當時倚之爲重，歷今千百歲，仰之曰「名臣」、曰「眞儒」，尚聞風而興起也。朱子，集諸儒之大成者。爾諸士資經術以靖獻，類宗朱子之說，以探聖經之蘊。觀其言，雖人人殊，要皆闡道德之奥，而盡義理之極者也。果能言行合一，終始不渝，存之足以修身而復性，推之足以尊
translation_en: … flourished into great domains of literature and learning. Speaking from this perspective, are men truly valued because of their homeland, or is a homeland valued because of its men? When we examine noble men such as Zhang Jiuling 張九齡, Fan Zhen 范鎮, Zhu Xi 朱熹, and Zhen Dexiu 眞德秀, they were indeed outstanding figures from Min 閩, Shu 蜀, and the Hundred Yue 百粵. In what they established and manifested, not only did their own times rely on them as pillars of importance, but even after hundreds and thousands of years down to the present, people look up to them, calling them "renowned ministers" and "true Confucians," and are still inspired upon hearing of their character. Master Zhu was the one who synthesized the great achievements of the various Confucian scholars. You scholars draw upon mastery of the classics to offer your loyal service, and you generally follow the doctrines of Master Zhu in order to fathom the profound depths of the sacred classics. Looking at your words, although they differ from person to person, in essence they all elucidate the mysteries of the Way and its virtue and exhaust the ultimate reaches of moral principle. If you can truly unite words and deeds, remaining steadfast from beginning to end, then preserving this within yourselves will suffice to cultivate your persons and restore your innate nature, while extending it outward will suffice to honor…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
主而庇民將輔世之烈名重泰山
擬則前修三代之英何遠焉
譬之連城照乘肇跡益遐天
下之珍重之也益至豈地之
所能限乎若乃借聖言以爲
邀爵之階取世榮而忘忠藎
之念是利祿之臣也即貴箴
===
之士亦羞與爲伍矣昔楚臣
論寶也謂聖能輔相國家則
寶之玉與珠能庇穀禦災則
寶之若夫譁囂之美非所寶
也而况乎珉之眩玉魚目之
眩珠也哉是故誠僞之分明
經者所當致辨而始進籍爲
punctuated: 主而庇民，將輔世之烈，名重泰山，擬則前修，三代之英何遠焉！譬之連城照乘，肇跡益遐，天下之珍重之也益至，豈地之所能限乎？若乃借聖言以爲邀爵之階，取世榮而忘忠藎之念，是利祿之臣也，即貴箴之士，亦羞與爲伍矣。昔楚臣論寶也，謂聖能輔相國家則寶之，玉與珠能庇穀禦災則寶之；若夫譁囂之美，非所寶也，而况乎珉之眩玉、魚目之眩珠也哉！是故誠僞之分，明經者所當致辨，而始進籍爲
translation_en: … honor the ruler and shelter the people, then their meritorious deeds in assisting the age will have a renown as weighty as Mount Tai. Modeling themselves on past worthies, how far off would the heroes of the Three Dynasties be? Take for example jade worth連城 (a string of cities) or pearls that 照乘 (illuminate carriages): the more distant their place of origin, the more supremely the world treasures and values them. How could they be limited by geography? If, however, one borrows the words of the sages as a stepping-stone to seek office and nobility, grasping at worldly glory while forgetting thoughts of loyal devotion, such a person is a minister out for profit and emolument; even the gentlemen of Guizhen [Guizhou] would be ashamed to be in his company. In antiquity, when the minister of Chu discussed treasures, he said that if a sage can assist the state, then he is treasured, and if jade and pearls can protect the grain and ward off disasters, then they are treasured; as for flashy and clamorous beauty, that is not what is treasured—and how much less so when common alabaster is passed off as jade, or fish eyes are passed off as pearls! Therefore, the distinction between sincerity and falsehood is what those who master the Classics ought to carefully discern, as they first enter the official register as…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
致身之準也孔子曰臣事君
以忠忠則誠而無僞矣〔登〕〔龍〕
不佞濫竽校文之役竊附於
以人事
君之義故惓惓以臣事
君之誂爲爾多士告於乎其共念
之哉是舉也前巡撫右僉都
===
御史嚴〔清〕夙敦文教遷秩甫
行今巡撫右僉都御史何〔起〕
鳴新奉
簡綸擁旄適至刑部郎中錢〔錫〕〔汝〕
總兵官署都督僉事吳〔國〕議
獄詰戎同有事於兹土右叅
政陳〔洙〕右叅議劉〔世〕〔賞〕梁〔士〕
punctuated:
致身之準也。孔子曰：「臣事君以忠。」忠則誠而無僞矣。〔登〕〔龍〕不佞，濫竽校文之役，竊附於以人事君之義，故惓惓以臣事君之誂，爲爾多士告。於乎！其共念之哉！

是舉也，前巡撫右僉都御史嚴〔清〕夙敦文教，遷秩甫行；今巡撫右僉都御史何〔起〕鳴新奉簡綸，擁旄適至；刑部郎中錢〔錫〕〔汝〕、總兵官署都督僉事吳〔國〕，議獄詰戎，同有事於兹土；右叅政陳〔洙〕、右叅議劉〔世〕〔賞〕、梁〔士〕
translation_en:
… the standard for devoting one's life to service. Confucius said, "A minister serves his ruler with loyalty." When one is loyal, one is sincere and without falsehood. Incompetent though I, [Denglong] 〔登〕〔龍〕, am, having unworthily filled a post in the task of evaluating examination papers, I have ventured to attach myself to the principle of serving the Sovereign by recommending men of talent; therefore, I earnestly address all of you scholars with this exhortation [? 誂, OCR for 義/道/誠] on how a minister serves his Sovereign. Oh, may you all bear this in mind together!

In this undertaking, the former Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Yan Qing 嚴〔清〕 had long fostered literary education and had just departed upon promotion to a new post; the current Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief He Qiming 何〔起〕鳴 newly received the imperial appointment and arrived bearing his standard of office just in time; Ministry of Justice Director Qian Xiru 錢〔錫〕〔汝〕 and Regional Commander and Acting Commissioner-in-Chief Wu Guo 吳〔國〕, deliberating on judicial cases and maintaining military readiness, were both engaged in official duties in this region; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Zhu 陳〔洙〕, Right Assistant Administration Commissioners Liu Shishang 劉〔世〕〔賞〕 and Liang Shi… 梁〔士〕…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
楚副使張守中楊起元僉事
王恩民署都指揮僉事許文
張奇峯右叅將侯之胄咸有
綜理防範之勞左叅議李□與
善僉事周汝德署都指揮僉
事楊仲雖預期入
賀亦嘗與聞其事者也法得併
===
書云
河南彰德府儒學教授顧登
龍謹序
punctuated:
楚，副使張守中、楊起元，僉事王恩民，署都指揮僉事許文、張奇峯，右叅將侯之胄，咸有綜理防範之勞。左叅議李□與善，僉事周汝德，署都指揮僉事楊仲，雖預期入賀，亦嘗與聞其事者也。法得併書云。
河南彰德府儒學教授顧登龍謹序。
translation_en:
…[Liang Shi]chu 梁士楚, Surveillance Vice Commissioners (副使) Zhang Shouzhong 張守中 and Yang Qiyuan 楊起元, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner (僉事) Wang Enmin 王恩民, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners (署都指揮僉事) Xu Wen 許文 and Zhang Qifeng 張奇峯, and Assistant Regional Commander of the Right (右叅將) Hou Zhizhou 侯之胄 all contributed their efforts in overall administration and security precautions. Left Assistant Administration Commissioner (左叅議) Li [?]yushan 李□與善 [likely Li Yushan 李與善, with an extraneous character], Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhou Rude 周汝德, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Yang Zhong 楊仲, although they had departed ahead of schedule to attend court for congratulations, had also previously participated in the planning of these affairs. ===
能通天下之志

利用安身以崇德也

punctuated:

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books (Sishu)

1. The Master said, "The gentleman takes rightness as his basic substance, puts it into practice by means of ritual propriety, expresses it with humility, and brings it to completion through trustworthiness. Such is a gentleman indeed!" (Analects 15.18)

2. Wherever heaven covers and earth sustains, wherever the sun and moon shine and the frost and dew fall, all who have blood and breath unfailingly honor and love him. (Doctrine of the Mean 31)

3. Drawing upon others to do good is helping others to do good. (Mencius 2A.8)

Book of Changes (Yi)

1. "Civilized and yet vigorous, central and correct and finding response: such is the correctness of the gentleman. Only the gentleman is able to comprehend the wills of all under heaven." (Hexagram 13, Tongren, Commentary on the Decision)

2. "Compliant and adhering to great brightness." (Hexagram 35, Jin, Commentary on the Decision)

3. "His knowledge encompasses all things, and his Way brings aid to all under heaven; therefore he does not err." (Appended Remarks, Part I, Ch. 4)

4. "Profiting from practical application and securing the person, thereby exalting virtue." (Appended Remarks, Part II, Ch. 5)

Book of Documents (Shu)

1. "It is virtue alone that moves Heaven; there is no distance to which it does not reach." ("Counsels of the Great Yu")

2. "Fix your thoughts from first to last constantly on learning, and your virtue will be cultivated without your being aware of it." ("Charge to Yue," Part III)

3. "Respectfulness produces seriousness; compliance produces orderliness; clear-sightedness produces wisdom; keenness of hearing produces deliberation; penetration produces sageliness." ("Great Plan")

4. "When you have good counsels and good plans, enter and announce them to your sovereign within, and then comply…" ("Jun Chen")

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
紀羣儒矣然周程張朱乃更爲道學傳
道學與儒果有二致歟當時稱道學與
朱熹鼎立爲三者顧道學傳又有與不
與何歟我
朝道隆化洽高出前古而翼運亮采諸臣勛
業爛焉後先相耀近世輯
皇明名臣言行錄固紀其樹立之偉以鳴
國家得人之盛矣或又摘其既錄者四人廣
其未錄者十一人各加論讃名之曰理
===
學云夫所謂理學者即宋之道學歟抑
造詣或有不同歟不知此外尚有默契
道體而可與數人竝傳者歟仰止前脩
士之上務也其詳言之以觀嚮往之素
問吾人立身宇宙間所謂耿耿不磨者維
忠與孝而已昔賢遺躅輝映史冊其大
節塞天地至行通神明者吾無議已特
其跡在可疑心未易白而論亦有難定
者試舉一二相與揚搉之漆身吞炭五
punctuated:
紀羣儒矣，然周、程、張、朱乃更爲《道學傳》。道學與儒果有二致歟？當時稱道學與朱熹鼎立爲三者，顧《道學傳》又有與不與，何歟？我朝道隆化洽，高出前古，而翼運亮采諸臣，勛業爛焉，後先相耀。近世輯《皇明名臣言行錄》，固紀其樹立之偉，以鳴國家得人之盛矣。或又摘其既錄者四人，廣其未錄者十一人，各加論讃，名之曰「理學」云。夫所謂理學者，即宋之道學歟？抑造詣或有不同歟？不知此外尚有默契道體，而可與數人竝傳者歟？仰止前脩，士之上務也。其詳言之，以觀嚮往之素。

translation_en:
…records the multitude of Confucians, yet for Zhou [Dunyi], the Cheng [brothers], Zhang [Zai], and Zhu [Xi], a separate "Biographies of the Learning of the Way" (Daoxue zhuan) was composed. Are the Learning of the Way and Confucianism truly two different things? Among those of that era who were acclaimed as standing alongside Zhu Xi like the three legs of a tripod in the Learning of the Way, some were included in the "Biographies of the Learning of the Way" and some were not; why is this?

In our August Dynasty, the Way flourishes and transformative teaching is pervasive, far surpassing antiquity, while the various ministers who assisted the dynastic fortune and displayed brilliant achievements have illustrious merits that shine upon one another in succession. In recent times, compilers have assembled the Record of Words and Deeds of Eminent Officials of the August Ming (Huang Ming mingchen yanxing lu), which indeed records the greatness of their accomplishments so as to proclaim the flourishing abundance of talent obtained by the state. Yet someone has further selected four men already recorded therein, expanded the list with eleven men not yet recorded, added critical appraisals and eulogies to each, and entitled it "The Learning of Principle" (Lixue). Now, is what is called the Learning of Principle the very same as the Song dynasty's Learning of the Way? Or are there perhaps differences in their scholarly attainments? Beyond these, do we know whether there are still others who silently apprehended the substance of the Way and deserve to have their biographies transmitted alongside these several men? Looking up in admiration to the worthy predecessors of the past is the foremost duty of a scholar. Expound upon this in detail, so that we may observe the abiding aspirations to which you incline.

The traces left behind by past worthies illuminate the pages of history. As for those whose great integrity fills heaven and earth and whose supreme conduct communicates with the spirits and gods, we have nothing to dispute regarding them. title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
起而不忘國士之報忠矣然晉陽之役
何頓忘三諫之規臨食舍肉一言而開
誓母之惑孝矣然伐許之舉何不能懲
一朝之忿挾吳成入郢之功復父讎也
然累世食君之祿可無念乎絕裾急江
左之行忠所事也然終身無復返之期
是可忍乎蕩陰之節高矣而忘情一本
之思其視誦詩興感而徵辟俱辭者孰
爲是也剖冰之行篤矣而甘心二姓之
===
事其視賦辭見志而丘園終身者孰爲
優也涉九折之坂而願忠願孝不同聞
貧母之招而從君從母或異斯皆古人
忠孝之跡也因跡以求心其得失亦有
可議者竭力致身之訓諸士子童而習
之久矣稽古之餘必有折衷之論幸詳
言之
問兵者所以威不軌而昭文德而將則三
軍之司命也顧用兵之法無常而將之
punctuated:
起而不忘國士之報，忠矣；然晉陽之役，何頓忘三諫之規？臨食舍肉，一言而開誓母之惑，孝矣；然伐許之舉，何不能懲一朝之忿？挾吳成入郢之功，復父讎也；然累世食君之祿，可無念乎？絕裾急江左之行，忠所事也；然終身無復返之期，是可忍乎？蕩陰之節高矣，而忘情一本之思，其視誦詩興感而徵辟俱辭者，孰爲是也？剖冰之行篤矣，而甘心二姓之事，其視賦辭見志而丘園終身者，孰爲優也？涉九折之坂，而願忠願孝不同；聞貧母之招，而從君從母或異。斯皆古人忠孝之跡也。因跡以求心，其得失亦有可議者。竭力致身之訓，諸士子童而習之久矣，稽古之餘，必有折衷之論，幸詳言之。

問：兵者，所以威不軌而昭文德，而將則三軍之司命也。顧用兵之法無常，而將之
translation_en:
…rising up five times without forgetting to repay the one who treated him as a scholar of statewide renown—that was loyal indeed; yet in the campaign at Jinyang, why did he suddenly forget the rule of remonstrating three times? Setting aside the meat at a meal and with a single word dispelling a ruler's delusion in swearing an oath against his mother—that was filial indeed; yet in the campaign to attack Xu, why could he not restrain a moment's anger? Relying on Wu to achieve the merit of entering Ying was to avenge a father's murder; yet when his family had for generations eaten the stipends of their lord, how could he give that no thought? Tearing away one's robe to hasten on a journey to Jiangzuo was to be loyal to the one he served; yet never having a time of return for the rest of his life—how could he bear to do this? The integrity shown at Dangyin was lofty indeed, yet he was oblivious to the longing for his own flesh and blood; compared with one who was moved upon reciting poetry and declined all summonses to office, which of them was in the right? The conduct of breaking the ice to catch carp was earnest indeed, yet he was content to serve two ruling houses; compared with one who composed a verse to show his resolve and remained in his country retreat for life, which of them was superior? In crossing the Nine-Turn Slope, one wished to be loyal and another wished to be filial, with different choices; in hearing the summons regarding an impoverished mother, one followed his lord and another followed his mother, with divergent paths. These are all the outward traces of loyalty and filial piety among the ancients. If we examine their inner intentions through their outward traces, their merits and failings also admit of discussion. The precepts of exerting one's utmost strength for parents and devoting one's life to the ruler have long been studied by you gentlemen since childhood. Beyond your investigation of antiquity, you must have balanced and judicious conclusions; please set them forth in detail.

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
材品亦未易辨宋人論將有賢將才將
之分而謂衛霍輩爲賢將韓信輩爲才
將其說果然歟數人皆非宿將一柄用
而動業爛然將何法以知之歟孫子論
兵奇正不可勝窮矣乃若召陵之役謂
或聚而爲正或分而爲奇唐之平淮西
也或以李光顏之據郾城爲正李愬之
襲蔡城爲奇其果然歟抑兵法卽正爲
奇卽奇爲正有不可以形泥歟苟兒六
===
術五權三至之論其於賢將才將何以
屬之魏相特著義兵應兵忿兵之目然
則奇正之變似又非所急與夫有文事
者必有武備諸士於此蘊之有素矣其
爲我詳言之毋諉曰軍旅未學
問漢開酒泉武威等四郡通道西域隔絕
羌與匈奴交援之路雄略至今賴之貴
州昔爲楚蜀徼外羈縻無專屬然實滇
越門户云前代不知疆理貴州故失滇
punctuated:
材品亦未易辨。宋人論將，有賢將、才將之分，而謂衛、霍輩爲賢將，韓信輩爲才將，其說果然歟？數人皆非宿將，一柄用而動業爛然，將何法以知之歟？孫子論兵，奇正不可勝窮矣。乃若召陵之役，謂或聚而爲正，或分而爲奇；唐之平淮西也，或以李光顏之據郾城爲正，李愬之襲蔡城爲奇，其果然歟？抑兵法卽正爲奇、卽奇爲正，有不可以形泥歟？苟兒六術、五權、三至之論，其於賢將、才將何以屬之？魏相特著義兵、應兵、忿兵之目，然則奇正之變似又非所急與？夫有文事者必有武備，諸士於此蘊之有素矣，其爲我詳言之，毋諉曰「軍旅未學」。
問：漢開酒泉、武威等四郡，通道西域，隔絕羌與匈奴交援之路，雄略至今賴之。貴州昔爲楚、蜀徼外，羈縻無專屬，然實滇、越門户云。前代不知疆理貴州，故失滇
translation_en:
… capacities and character are also not easy to discern. When scholars of the Song dynasty discussed generals, they distinguished between "worthy generals" (xianjiang) and "talented generals" (caijiang), claiming that men like Wei Qing 衛青 and Huo Qubing 霍去病 were worthy generals, while men like Han Xin 韓信 were talented generals. Is this view truly so? None of these several men were veteran generals, yet once entrusted with command, their achievements [OCR: 動 for 勳] shone brilliantly—by what method could one have known their abilities beforehand? When Master Sun 孫子 discussed warfare, the permutations of the unorthodox (qi) and the orthodox (zheng) were inexhaustible. Yet regarding the campaign of Shaoling 召陵, it is said that some forces gathered to serve as the orthodox while others divided to serve as the unorthodox; and in the Tang pacification of Huaixi 淮西, some regarded Li Guangyan's 李光顏 occupation of Yancheng 郾城 as the orthodox and Li Su's 李愬 surprise attack on Caicheng 蔡城 as the unorthodox. Is this truly so? Or is it that in the art of war, the orthodox itself becomes the unorthodox and the unorthodox itself becomes the orthodox, such that one cannot be bound by fixed forms? As for Master Xun's 荀子 [OCR: 苟兒 for 荀卿] discourse on the "six arts" (liushu), "five balances" (wuquan), and "three supremacies" (sanzhi) of generalship, how do these correspond to worthy generals and talented generals? Wei Xiang 魏相 specifically set forth the categories of "armies of righteousness" (yibing), "armies of response" (yingbing), and "armies of resentment" (fenbing); if so, do the transformations of the unorthodox and the orthodox seem not to be of primary urgency after all? Now, whoever has civil affairs must also have military preparations. You gentlemen have long cultivated your understanding of these matters; expound upon them in detail for me, and do not excuse yourselves by saying, "Military affairs I have not learned."

In the past, Guizhou 貴州 lay beyond the frontiers of Chu 楚 and Shu 蜀, held only under loose rein (jimi) without fixed jurisdiction, yet it was truly called the gateway to Dian 滇 [Yunnan] and Yue 越. title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
中沃野之利而南詔憑險跳梁爲中國
邊鄙患歷宋而未艾也我
太祖將廓清雲南先經略貴州肇建都司制普
定牂牁阻深之區也戍聯絡亭障相望
諸夷帖伏山谷稱雄鎮焉
成祖因田宗鼎輩擅兵相攻旣寘之法遂緝其
地建藩臬諸司稱埒十三省民庶寖謐
文教聿興大一統之盛蓋開闢所未有
也豈特與漢之開酒泉等郡比烈哉然
===
承平日久蠹耗日生亡論戍兵單弱即
編氓亦日就凋敝點夷乘間竊發每厪
當事者之憂而說者則謂長養招徠最
爲今急務其果然歟考之漢時趙充國
留屯湟中上便宜十二策四郡卒賴其
利今度貴州道里之形及坡阪民所未
墾類與酒泉無異昔人募民實塞及就
草爲田之策有可率而行者乎抑久安
長治之略固不止於此也多士生長其
punctuated: 中沃野之利，而南詔憑險跳梁，爲中國邊鄙患，歷宋而未艾也。我太祖將廓清雲南，先經略貴州，肇建都司，制普定、牂牁阻深之區，也戍聯絡，亭障相望，諸夷帖伏，山谷稱雄鎮焉。成祖因田宗鼎輩擅兵相攻，旣寘之法，遂緝其地，建藩、臬諸司，稱埒十三省，民庶寖謐，文教聿興，大一統之盛，蓋開闢所未有也，豈特與漢之開酒泉等郡比烈哉？然承平日久，蠹耗日生，亡論戍兵單弱，即編氓亦日就凋敝，點夷乘間竊發，每厪當事者之憂。而說者則謂長養、招徠最爲今急務，其果然歟？考之漢時，趙充國留屯湟中，上便宜十二策，四郡卒賴其利。今度貴州道里之形，及坡阪民所未墾，類與酒泉無異。昔人募民實塞，及就草爲田之策，有可率而行者乎？抑久安長治之略，固不止於此也？多士生長其
translation_en:
… the benefit of the fertile plains of central Dian, while Nanzhao relied on its rugged terrain to rebel, becoming a scourge along China's frontier that continued unabated through the Song dynasty. When Our Taizu was about to pacify and clear Yunnan, he first planned the administration of Guizhou, initiating the establishment of the Regional Military Commission to control the remote and rugged regions of Puding and Zangke. With garrisons [?] linked together and frontier outposts within sight of one another, the various non-Chinese tribes submitted docilely, and these mountain valleys were acclaimed as a mighty stronghold. Because Tian Zongding 田宗鼎 and his cohorts unauthorizedly took up arms and attacked one another, Chengzu subjected them to the law, subsequently brought order to their lands, and established the Provincial Administration Commission, the Provincial Surveillance Commission, and other agencies, ranking it on par with the thirteen provinces. The common people gradually enjoyed peace and tranquillity, and literary culture and education flourished. Such grandeur of great unification had indeed never been seen since the creation of the world—how could it merely be compared in merit with the Han dynasty's opening of Jiuquan and the other commanderies?

Yet after a long period of peace, abuses and depletion arise daily. Not to mention that the garrison troops are thin and weak, even the registered commoners are growing more destitute by the day. Crafty [?] tribesmen seize opportunities to break out in secret, constantly causing anxiety for those in authority. Commentators, however, maintain that nurturing the populace and attracting settlers are the most urgent tasks today—is this truly so? Examining the Han period, Zhao Chongguo 趙充國 remained to establish military agricultural colonies in Huangzhong and submitted twelve proposals on advantageous measures, from whose benefits the four commanderies ultimately profited. Today, if we assess the configuration of distances and roads in Guizhou, as well as the slopes and hillsides not yet cultivated by the people, they are largely no different from those of Jiuquan. Can the policies of men of the past—recruiting commoners to populate the frontiers and turning grasslands into cultivated fields—be followed and put into practice here? title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰君子義以爲質禮以行之孫以出之
信以成之君子哉
孫思述
同考試官教諭謝　批　義禮孫信總是一理則四言之文有歸
趣士子類能成文孫少體認是作說理詳明而措詞穩貼宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳　批　深得夫子立言之意是蓋於斯者錄之
考試官教授顧　批　說理之文允稱多士
===
聖人詳君子制事之道而深與之也夫主之以
義而禮孫信以濟之制事之道盡矣不謂之君
子哉夫子示人之意若曰天下之事本有定理
而人之處事恒無全能其惟君子乎知事無常
形而裁制之在吾心者卽謂之義也于是隨事
以觀理而其行其止惟以義權之也虛心以順
應而或從或違惟以義斷之也一義立而事之
質幹具矣由是而行之必以禮焉品節詳明俾
協乎嘉會之則而不至過乎中也出之必以孫
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「子曰：『君子義以爲質，禮以行之，孫以出之，信以成之。君子哉！』」
孫思述
同考試官教諭謝　批：義、禮、孫、信總是一理，則四言之文有歸趣。士子類能成文，孫少體認；是作說理詳明，而措詞穩貼，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭陳　批：深得夫子立言之意，是蓋於斯者，錄之。
考試官教授顧　批：說理之文，允稱多士。
聖人詳君子制事之道，而深與之也。夫主之以義，而禮、孫、信以濟之，制事之道盡矣，不謂之君子哉？夫子示人之意，若曰：天下之事本有定理，而人之處事恒無全能，其惟君子乎！知事無常形，而裁制之在吾心者，卽謂之義也。于是隨事以觀理，而其行其止，惟以義權之也；虛心以順應，而或從或違，惟以義斷之也。一義立而事之質幹具矣。由是而行之必以禮焉，品節詳明，俾協乎嘉會之則，而不至過乎中也；出之必以孫…
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books
"The Master said: 'The gentleman takes rightness as his substance, puts it into practice with ritual propriety, brings it forth with humility, and brings it to completion with trustworthiness. A gentleman indeed!'" (Analects 15.18)
By Sun Sishu.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xie: Rightness, ritual propriety, humility, and trustworthiness are altogether a single principle; only when one grasps this do the words of the four clauses have a unified aim. Candidates can generally compose an essay on this, yet lack personal realization [Reading 孫 as 遜/鮮?]. This composition explains the principles with clarity and detail, and its phrasing is apt and well-grounded; it should be selected as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Chen: He has deeply grasped the Master's intention in establishing these words; he is one who is truly devoted to this [?]. Selected.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Gu: An essay that explicates principle, truly worthy of leading the many scholars.
The sage sets forth in detail the gentleman's way of handling affairs and deeply commends him. When one makes rightness the master and complements it with ritual propriety, humility, and trustworthiness, the way of handling affairs is exhausted—must we not call him a gentleman? In instructing others, the Master's meaning was to say: The affairs of the world inherently have fixed principles, yet in managing affairs people constantly lack complete capability—is it not only the gentleman who possesses it! He knows that affairs have no constant form, and that what regulates and adjudicates them within our mind is precisely what is called rightness. Therefore, he observes principle in accordance with each affair, and whether to advance or to halt, he weighs it solely by rightness; he responds with an open mind, and whether to follow or to oppose, he decides it solely by rightness. Once rightness is established, the substantial trunk of the affair is complete. From this, in putting it into practice, he necessarily does so with ritual propriety—making its grades and distinctions clear and detailed, so that it accords with the standard of harmonious assemblage and does not exceed the mean; in bringing it forth, he necessarily does so with humility…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
焉從容不迫俾適乎退讓之休而不至失於矯
也成之必以信焉以實心任實事俾始終皆一
誠之貫徹而不至失之僞也夫義以爲質則適
莫不存運於心者既有定準禮行孫出信成則
中和交濟措於用者又有全能一事而衆善備
焉是謂慮善以動君子所以酬酢萬變而行無
不利者胥此也一動而衆理該焉是謂以理應
事君子所以經綸天下而推無不準者胥此也
謂之曰君子哉信非夫人之所能與矣欲處事
===
者可不以是爲則哉抑四者信處事之要矣夫
子他日又獨曰義之與比何哉蓋義其本也禮
孫信特以善其用於不偏耳使義有不立雖有
禮孫信欲施之得其當難矣易稱精義入神以
致用夫精義而至於入神則於禮孫信一以貫
之矣其於致用何有然則欲以義而制事者其
必有精義之學而後可
天之所覆地之所載日月所照霜露所隊
凡有血氣者莫不尊親
punctuated:
焉，從容不迫，俾適乎退讓之休，而不至失於矯也；成之必以信焉，以實心任實事，俾始終皆一誠之貫徹，而不至失之僞也。夫義以爲質，則適莫不存，運於心者既有定準；禮行、孫出、信成，則中和交濟，措於用者又有全能。一事而衆善備焉，是謂「慮善以動」，君子所以酬酢萬變而行無不利者，胥此也；一動而衆理該焉，是謂以理應事，君子所以經綸天下而推無不準者，胥此也。謂之曰「君子哉」，信非夫人之所能與矣！欲處事者，可不以是爲則哉？抑四者信處事之要矣，夫子他日又獨曰「義之與比」，何哉？蓋義，其本也；禮、孫、信，特以善其用於不偏耳。使義有不立，雖有禮、孫、信，欲施之得其當，難矣。《易》稱：「精義入神，以致用。」夫精義而至於入神，則於禮、孫、信一以貫之矣，其於致用何有？然則欲以義而制事者，其必有精義之學而後可。

天之所覆，地之所載，日月所照，霜露所隊，凡有血氣者，莫不尊親。
translation_en:
…being unhurried and unforced, so that it accords with the beauty of modest yielding and does not err by becoming affected; and he brings it to completion unfailingly with trustworthiness, undertaking real affairs with a genuine heart, so that from beginning to end a single sincerity pervades it all and it does not err by becoming false. Now, when righteousness is taken as the substance, neither arbitrary predisposition nor rigid aversion remains, and what operates in the mind already has a fixed standard; when it is practiced with ritual propriety, expressed with humility, and completed with trustworthiness, equilibrium and harmony mutually reinforce one another, and what is put into practice possesses complete capability. When in a single affair all virtues are present, this is what is called "deliberating on the good before acting"—that whereby the gentleman responds to ten thousand changes and acts without anything failing to be advantageous is entirely through this. When in a single action all principles are encompassed, this is what is called responding to affairs with principle—that whereby the gentleman orders the world and extends his measures without anything failing to be accurate is entirely through this. To call him "A gentleman indeed!"—truly this is not something that just any man can partake in! For those who wish to manage affairs, how could they not take this as their model? Yet while these four are indeed the essentials of managing affairs, on another day the Master spoke solely of "aligning oneself with righteousness"—why is that? Because righteousness is the root; ritual propriety, humility, and trustworthiness merely perfect its application so that it does not lean to one side. Suppose righteousness is not established: even if one has ritual propriety, humility, and trustworthiness, and wishes to apply them appropriately, it would be difficult. The Book of Changes (Yi) states: "Refining righteousness to the point of entering the numinous, in order to attain practical application." Now, when one refines righteousness until it enters the numinous, then ritual propriety, humility, and trustworthiness are threaded together by a single principle—what difficulty would there be in attaining practical application? That being so, one who wishes to regulate affairs through righteousness must first possess the learning that refines righteousness, and only then will it be possible.

Wherever heaven covers, wherever earth sustains, wherever the sun and moon shine, wherever frost and dew fall: among all who have blood and breath, there is none who does not honor and love him.

哉箕子演之以告武王若曰五事之在人也蘊

亦妙於自然是故貌之德曰恭恭非有期于肅

疏觀不蔽者其體也以之燭理則彰往察來見

有感卽通非聞見之所能囿至靈達乎幽隱而
有觸卽應非方體之所能拘肅乂哲謀之理蓋
一以貫之矣聖之無不通者又非睿通乎微者
爲之乎夫五德藴于中而其用見於外皆身之
所全具者也人君敬以修之其於誠身也何有
抑論修五事而必曰敬者蓋敬統動靜而一之
也靜而能敬則有主而虛而德可立動而能敬
則外物不累而用可行然其動也常本乎靜而
持敬者必自靜始故又曰聖人主靜立人極
===
詩
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播百
穀
考試官敎諭陳　批　沈　權
理明而確詞婉而莊
考試官教授顧　批
模寫幽人勤農重本之意典雅懇
到詩義之佳者宜冠多士
豳民勤趨乎治室之務者將慮乎農事之興也
甚矣民事不可緩也若待時之已迫則不暇爲
punctuated:
有感卽通，非聞見之所能囿；至靈達乎幽隱，而有觸卽應，非方體之所能拘。肅、乂、哲、謀之理，蓋一以貫之矣。聖之無不通者，又非睿通乎微者爲之乎？夫五德藴于中，而其用見於外，皆身之所全具者也。人君敬以修之，其於誠身也何有？抑論修五事而必曰「敬」者，蓋敬統動靜而一之也。靜而能敬，則有主而虛，而德可立；動而能敬，則外物不累，而用可行。然其動也常本乎靜，而持敬者必自靜始，故又曰：「聖人主靜立人極。」

詩：「晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。」

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
王繩武之效而實武王垂後之休有以裕之也
此其爲可頌歟雖然亦在後人世守何如耳故
啓賢能敬而後夏之典則爲弗墜而上帝是皇
奄有四方誦成康之德不衰也嗚呼使繩祖武
者世有人焉則天命人心久而愈固周雖至今
存可也夫何菀柳之刺興而下武之詩絶響矣
然則籍祖宗垂裕之澤其可忘繼述之思哉
春秋
春王正月公敗齊師于長勺莊公十年冬
===
公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月己亥同盟于戲襄公九年公會
晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾
子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭
魚襄公十有一年晉士匄帥師侵齊至
穀乃還襄公十有九年夏六月庚申公
會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子盟于澶淵
punctuated:
王繩武之效，而實武王垂後之休有以裕之也，此其爲可頌歟！雖然，亦在後人世守何如耳。故啓賢能敬，而後夏之典則爲弗墜；而「上帝是皇，奄有四方」，誦成、康之德不衰也。嗚呼！使「繩祖武」者世有人焉，則天命人心久而愈固，周雖至今存可也。夫何《菀柳》之刺興，而《下武》之詩絶響矣！然則籍祖宗垂裕之澤，其可忘繼述之思哉？

《春秋》
「春，王正月，公敗齊師于長勺。」（莊公十年）「冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲。」（襄公九年）「公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。會于蕭魚。」（襄公十有一年）「晉士匄帥師侵齊，至穀，乃還。」（襄公十有九年）「夏，六月庚申，公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子盟于澶淵。」
translation_en:
…the efficacy of the later kings' following in his martial footsteps, yet in reality it was made abundant by the blessings King Wu bequeathed to posterity. Is this not worthy of eulogy? Even so, it also depends on how descendants guard it from generation to generation. Thus, only because Qi was worthy and able to be reverent did the statutes and models of Xia not fall into ruin; and with "the Sovereign on High being august, they grandly possessed the four quarters," the praises of the virtue of Kings Cheng and Kang never waned. Alas! Had there been in every generation men who "followed in the footsteps of their ancestors," then the Mandate of Heaven and the hearts of the people would have grown ever more secure with time, and the Zhou might well have survived even to this day. Why, then, did the satire of the ode "Luxuriant Willow" (Wanliu) arise, and the echoes of the ode "Continuing the Martial" (Xiawu) die away? This being so, when relying on the abundant blessings bequeathed by one's ancestors, how could one forget the thought of continuing and carrying forward their work?

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"In spring, in the King's first month, the Duke defeated the army of Qi at Changshao." (10th year of Duke Zhuang) "In winter, the Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Little Zhu, and Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi, to attack Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the day jihai, they made a covenant together at Xi." (9th year of Duke Xiang) "The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, Heir Apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu to attack Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu." (11th year of Duke Xiang) "Shi Gai of Jin led a force to raid Qi; having reached Gu, he then turned back." (19th year of Duke Xiang) "In summer, in the sixth month, on the day gengshen, the Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu, and made a covenant at Chanyuan."…

楚勢則益張矣使將非親行師非厚集抑何以
挫强梁之勢拯危急之患哉幸而景也躬統三

上下與天地同流如此此王道之所以爲大也
歟抑論聖人參天地賛化育惟其誠而已誠者
造化之樞聖人之本也使聖德少有不誠其何
足以配天乎德不足以配天其足稱天之宗子
乎然則天厚聖人而錫以德位之全者正欲其
裁成輔相使人物各得其所也故曰聖人天地
之用

論

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
物不遂其生者天地萬物皆吾度內而無外之
仁如是也然其道曷甞不求端於天乎是故天
之覆幬無外而聖人民胞物與之量亦至大而
無外天之生成無私而聖人所以仁育義正于
一世者亦至公而不私使有私焉則理窒而不
通量窄而不廣非所以語於一體之仁矣公者
正也正所以成其大也聖王以純王之心行純
王之政而德業與天地同流夫豈私意小智之
所能及哉人主當以天下爲度胡氏其知言矣
===
請得而論之今夫天下之廣兆民之衆廣谷大
川謠俗若是其不同華夏蠻貊族類若是其不
一而聖人者固亦人類中之一人耳乃獨膺寵
綏之寄上而爲天地之宗子下而爲億兆之元
后總一海內宰制六合威命靈爽侔乎造化豈
特以崇高之勢而懾服之哉實以大公之度聯
屬于天下而與天爲一耳何也天地之大德曰
生而其道則包含徧覆而無所擇陰陽寒暑之
迭運震曜慘舒之異施要其歸使品物保合於
punctuated:
物不遂其生者，天地萬物皆吾度內，而無外之仁如是也。然其道曷甞不求端於天乎？是故天之覆幬無外，而聖人民胞物與之量亦至大而無外；天之生成無私，而聖人所以仁育義正于一世者亦至公而不私。使有私焉，則理窒而不通，量窄而不廣，非所以語於一體之仁矣。公者，正也，正所以成其大也。聖王以純王之心，行純王之政，而德業與天地同流，夫豈私意小智之所能及哉！「人主當以天下爲度」，胡氏其知言矣。請得而論之。
今夫天下之廣，兆民之衆，廣谷大川，謠俗若是其不同；華夏蠻貊，族類若是其不一。而聖人者，固亦人類中之一人耳。乃獨膺寵綏之寄，上而爲天地之宗子，下而爲億兆之元后，總一海內，宰制六合，威命靈爽，侔乎造化，豈特以崇高之勢而懾服之哉？實以大公之度聯屬于天下，而與天爲一耳。何也？天地之大德曰生，而其道則包含徧覆而無所擇，陰陽寒暑之迭運，震曜慘舒之異施，要其歸，使品物保合於
translation_en:
…living thing fails to fulfill its life—heaven, earth, and the myriad things are all within one's measure, and such is the benevolence that excludes nothing as outside. Yet how could this Way ever fail to seek its origin in Heaven? Therefore, just as Heaven's overarching canopy excludes nothing, the sage's capacity to regard the people as his kin and creatures as his companions is likewise supremely great and excludes nothing; just as Heaven gives birth and completion without partiality, the means by which the sage nurtures with benevolence and rectifies with righteousness throughout the world is likewise supremely impartial and without selfishness. Were there any selfishness in it, principle would be obstructed and unable to flow through, and his capacity would be narrow rather than broad—this would be no way to speak of the benevolence that forms a single body with all things. Impartiality is rectitude, and rectitude is that by which greatness is achieved. The sage-king, with the heart of a pure king, carries out the governance of a pure king, so that his virtue and achievements flow together with Heaven and Earth; how could selfish intentions and petty cleverness ever attain to this! "The ruler of men ought to take all under Heaven as his measure"—Master Hu (Hu Yin 胡寅) truly knew how to speak of this. Allow me to discuss it.

Now, consider the vastness of all under Heaven and the multitude of the millions of people: across broad valleys and great rivers, songs and customs are thus so diverse; among the civilized states of Huaxia and the Man and Mo tribes, clans and kinds are thus so varied. Yet the sage is, after all, merely one person among humankind. That he alone receives the charge to favor and pacify them—above acting as the eldest son of Heaven and Earth, below acting as the supreme sovereign of the millions—unifying all within the seas, governing the six directions, his awesome mandate and numinous vigor matching the creative power of nature: how could it be merely by the power of his exalted position that he overawes them into submission? In truth, it is by the measure of great impartiality that he binds together all under Heaven and becomes one with Heaven. Why is this? The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life-giving, and its Way is to encompass and shelter everything universally without discrimination; yin and yang, cold and heat alternate in their revolutions, and thunder, lightning, gloom, and clear weather are differently bestowed, yet in the final analysis, all of this is simply to cause the myriad things to preserve and harmonize in…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
太和而已矣聖人之大德曰仁而其道亦溥愛
容保而無所偏敎養政治之兼舉慶賞刑威之
竝行要其歸使萬民允升於大猷而已矣是故
昊天之盡物者以其普萬物而無心也聖人之
盡民者以其順萬事而無情也知天地則知聖
人矣蓋聞善言天者莫辯於易故於復見天地
之心於正大見天地之情而於遏惡揚善則以
爲順天休命焉於此見天之未始不爲人也善
言人者莫辯於書洪範之皇極無作好而遵道
===
無作惡而遵路而庶徵之應乃與天地流通焉
於此見人之未始不爲天也董仲舒則謂王者
承天意以從事故任德而不任刑嗚呼刑固不
可任而亦不可廢也曷不自天道聖人之全者
觀之乎是故陽居春夏以養育而生乎物也王
者繼天而爲之子則有賞賞以勸善非私喜而
作好也善人天地之紀天之所福也五服五章
順天而命有德耳陰居秋冬以肅殺而成乎物
也王者繼天而爲之子則有刑刑以懲惡非私
punctuated: 太和而已矣。聖人之大德曰仁，而其道亦溥愛容保而無所偏；敎養政治之兼舉，慶賞刑威之竝行，要其歸，使萬民允升於大猷而已矣。是故昊天之盡物者，以其普萬物而無心也；聖人之盡民者，以其順萬事而無情也。知天地則知聖人矣。蓋聞善言天者莫辯於《易》，故於《復》見天地之心，於正大見天地之情，而於遏惡揚善則以爲順天休命焉，於此見天之未始不爲人也；善言人者莫辯於《書》，《洪範》之皇極，無作好而遵道，無作惡而遵路，而庶徵之應乃與天地流通焉，於此見人之未始不爲天也。董仲舒則謂「王者承天意以從事，故任德而不任刑」。嗚呼！刑固不可任，而亦不可廢也，曷不自天道聖人之全者觀之乎？是故陽居春夏，以養育而生乎物也；王者繼天而爲之子，則有賞。賞以勸善，非私喜而作好也；善人，天地之紀，天之所福也，五服五章，順天而命有德耳。陰居秋冬，以肅殺而成乎物也；王者繼天而爲之子，則有刑。刑以懲惡，非私…
translation_en:
…supreme harmony, and nothing more. The great virtue of the Sage is called benevolence, and his Way likewise extends universal love and tolerant protection without partiality; through the joint undertaking of instruction, nourishment, and governance, and the parallel application of rewards and punishments, the ultimate aim is simply to enable the myriad people truly to ascend to the grand plan, and nothing more. Therefore, vast Heaven fulfills the nature of all things because it reaches the myriad things universally and without deliberate mind; the Sage fulfills the nature of the people because he accords with the myriad affairs without personal sentiment. To understand Heaven and Earth is thus to understand the Sage.

Indeed, I have heard that in speaking well of Heaven, nothing is more discerning than the Classic of Changes (Yi): thus in the hexagram Return (Fu) one sees the mind of Heaven and Earth, in uprightness and greatness one sees the disposition of Heaven and Earth, and in repressing evil and promoting good one regards it as obeying the beneficent mandate of Heaven—herein we see that Heaven has never failed to act for the sake of man. In speaking well of man, nothing is more discerning than the Classic of Documents (Shu): in the "Supreme Standard" (Huangji) of the "Great Plan" (Hongfan), one indulges in no personal favoritism and follows the Way, indulges in no personal animosity and follows the Royal Road, and the responses of the "Various Verifications" (Shuzheng) thereupon communicate seamlessly with Heaven and Earth—herein we see that man has never failed to act as Heaven.

Dong Zhongshu, however, maintained that "a true king carries out his affairs by receiving the intent of Heaven, and therefore relies on virtue rather than punishment." Alas! While punishment certainly should not be relied upon exclusively, neither can it be abolished. Why not examine this from the entirety of the Way of Heaven and the Sage? Therefore, yang resides in spring and summer to nourish and give life to things; the true king succeeds Heaven as its Son, and thus institutes rewards. Rewards are used to encourage the good, not to indulge in private joy or personal favoritism. Good men are the mainstay of Heaven and Earth and those whom Heaven blesses; the five ceremonial vestments and their five insignia are simply obeying Heaven in conferring mandate upon the virtuous. Yin resides in autumn and winter to bring things to completion through stern withering; the true king succeeds Heaven as its Son, and thus institutes punishments. Punishments are used to chastise evil, not out of private…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
怒而作惡也惡人棄天之性天之所禍也五刑
五用順天而討有罪耳夫聖人之治天下也本
之心德施之化導委之常秩樹之表儀非區區
於賞刑之加而賞刑其樞要也是賞刑也原之
爲喜怒之情順之爲中和之理制之爲詔爵詔
祿奪食之恩黜遠梏拲斬戮之典達之爲爵人
而與衆共刑人而與衆棄皆因人而施隨施而
當人主如鑑空衡平而一巳之私無與焉此其
心誠有視我惟天地萬物而內忘乎巳視天地
===
萬物惟我而外忘乎物體正大之情得其所以
生物之心而合天下以爲度者也存之無偏無
黨有以立王道之體焉發之無反無側有以著
王道之用焉感之會極歸極有以溥王道之化
焉是故以是而正之朝廷則濟濟彬諧之風行
矣而巧言者爲之化而忠也邪辟者爲之化而
廉也而臣于是乎無比德矣以是而正之萬民
則興仁興讓之風行矣而暴慢者爲之化而恭
也狡猾者爲之化而順也而民於是乎無淫行
punctuated: 怒而作惡也。惡人，棄天之性，天之所禍也；五刑五用，順天而討有罪耳。夫聖人之治天下也，本之心德，施之化導，委之常秩，樹之表儀，非區區於賞刑之加，而賞刑其樞要也。是賞刑也，原之爲喜怒之情，順之爲中和之理，制之爲詔爵、詔祿、奪食之恩，黜遠、梏拲、斬戮之典，達之爲爵人而與衆共、刑人而與衆棄，皆因人而施，隨施而當。人主如鑑空衡平，而一巳之私無與焉。此其心誠有視我惟天地萬物而內忘乎巳，視天地萬物惟我而外忘乎物，體正大之情，得其所以生物之心，而合天下以爲度者也。存之無偏無黨，有以立王道之體焉；發之無反無側，有以著王道之用焉；感之會極歸極，有以溥王道之化焉。是故以是而正之朝廷，則濟濟彬諧之風行矣，而巧言者爲之化而忠也，邪辟者爲之化而廉也，而臣于是乎無比德矣。以是而正之萬民，則興仁興讓之風行矣，而暴慢者爲之化而恭也，狡猾者爲之化而順也，而民於是乎無淫行
translation_en: …anger or acting out of malice. The wicked abandon the nature endowed by Heaven, and thus they are whom Heaven brings disaster upon; the five punishments in their five applications merely follow Heaven in chastising the guilty. Now, when the sage governs the world, he roots his rule in the virtue of the mind, implements it through transformative guidance, entrusts it to regular offices, and establishes standards of model conduct. He is not narrowly preoccupied with the mere meting out of rewards and punishments, yet rewards and punishments are the pivot of governance. As for these rewards and punishments, traced to their source, they are the emotions of joy and anger; harmonized with principle, they are the states of equilibrium and harmony; institutionalized, they become the favors of conferring rank, bestowing emoluments, and granting sustenance [?], as well as the statutes of dismissal and banishment, fettering and shackling, and execution; extended in practice, they mean conferring rank upon men in accord with the public and punishing men by casting them out in accord with the public. All are applied according to the person, and in every application they are fitting. The ruler is like an empty mirror and a level balance, with no selfish partiality of his own involved therein. Truly, his mind views the self as one with Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, inwardly forgetting himself; and views Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one with the self, outwardly forgetting things—embodying upright and magnanimous sentiments, attaining the very mind by which Heaven and Earth give life to things, and uniting the whole world as his measure. Preserving this mind without偏 (partiality) or 黨 (partisanship), he thereby establishes the substance of the Kingly Way; manifesting it without perversity or one-sidedness, he thereby displays the function of the Kingly Way; moving others so that they converge upon and return to the Supreme Standard, he thereby makes universal the transformation of the Kingly Way. Therefore, when by this means he rectifies the court, an ethos of dignified harmony prevails: those of artful words are transformed by it and become loyal, the perverse and depraved are transformed by it and become upright, and ministers thereupon are free of factious conduct. When by this means he rectifies the myriad people, an ethos of rising benevolence and yielding courtesy prevails: the violent and arrogant are transformed by it and become respectful, the crafty and deceitful are transformed by it and become obedient, and the people thereupon are free of licentious deeds…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
聖朝之御臨方志同以成泰講讀推褚量之博
廹邢昺而經術益醇諫議仰魏徵之賢至
田錫而忠讜愈著況玉堂
賜篆光聯重金之榮兩省綴班先沐五品之
貺休兹
熙朝之盛事詎意愚臣之濫膺覥顔班行耤
爲致身之始矢心就列敢忘報國之忱兹
蓋伏遇
○○○○
===
英姿天挺
聖敬日躋
擴至仁以安民
躬大孝而繼志
悉蠲新法海宇沐行葦之恩
隆禮耆儒楷紳詠卷阿之盛庶政已登諸理
益懷永圖羣賢咸聚於
朝尤切好問惟慎簡首尊於宿德故旁求誤
及於虛名臣祖禹性惟質戇學本膚庸史
punctuated: 聖朝之御臨，方志同以成泰。講讀推褚量之博，廹邢昺而經術益醇；諫議仰魏徵之賢，至田錫而忠讜愈著。況玉堂賜篆，光聯重金之榮；兩省綴班，先沐五品之貺。休兹熙朝之盛事，詎意愚臣之濫膺。覥顔班行，耤爲致身之始；矢心就列，敢忘報國之忱。兹蓋伏遇○○○○，英姿天挺，聖敬日躋。擴至仁以安民，躬大孝而繼志。悉蠲新法，海宇沐《行葦》之恩；隆禮耆儒，楷紳詠《卷阿》之盛。庶政已登諸理，益懷永圖；羣賢咸聚於朝，尤切好問。惟慎簡首尊於宿德，故旁求誤及於虛名。臣祖禹性惟質戇，學本膚庸。史
translation_en:
…the governance of our Sacred Dynasty, just when hearts are united to bring about peace and prosperity. Among Exposition and Reader-in-Waiting officials, Chu Liang (褚亮, written 褚量) was praised for his erudition, and by the time of Xing Bing (邢昺) classicist scholarship grew ever purer; among Policy Critics, Wei Zheng (魏徵) was revered for his worthiness, and down to Tian Xi (田錫) loyal and forthright counsel became ever more manifest. How much more so when the Jade Hall bestows its seal-script commission, its splendor linked to the honor of double gold; and joining the ranks of the Two Chancellery-Secretariats, one is first bathed in the favor of the fifth rank! Splendid is this grand affair of a flourishing court—how could Your foolish servant have expected to unworthily receive it? With abashed countenance in the court ranks, I take this as the beginning of devoting my life to service; swearing in my heart as I take my place, how would I dare forget my sincere desire to repay the state?

This is because I humbly encounter Your Majesty [○○○○], whose heroic bearing is heaven-endowed, and whose sacred reverence ascends daily. You expand utmost benevolence to give peace to the people, and personally practice great filial piety to carry on the ancestral will. Completely abolishing the New Laws, the realm within the seas is bathed in the grace of the ode "Roadside Reeds" (Xingwei); treating aged Confucian scholars with exalted courtesy, the gentry sing of the flourishing of the ode "Curving Hill" (Juan'e). All affairs of government have already been brought to order, yet You ever more cherish far-reaching plans; all the worthies are gathered at Court, yet You are ever more earnest in loving to inquire. Because Your careful selection first honors venerable virtue, Your broad search has mistakenly extended to one of empty reputation. Your servant Zuyu (Fan Zuyu 范祖禹) is by nature merely simple and blunt, and in learning fundamentally shallow and commonplace. In history…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
從諫水之緒廑僅能觀成敗之迹經出程
門之指授卒未究賢聖之精昔棲遲而括
囊今遭遇以疇祉清切之地愧非才賢之
居負秉之蕘誓竭贊襄之力直言國體罔
擇五術之工殫究道眞奚資七盛之詑遠
稽十漸近取五規法處厚關雎之陳學孫
奭無逸之解倘進德愛身之疏如可底行
庶責難陳善之恭不爲虛語伏願
心純乾健
===
德懋晉昭
謨訓爲定保之徵罔以側言而改度
紀綱敦愷悌之美恒持宥密而執中
信順誕敷于九圍
瑤圖益固
文明光被于四表
寶曆彌昌臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹奉
punctuated: 從諫水之緒廑，僅能觀成敗之迹；經出程門之指授，卒未究賢聖之精。昔棲遲而括囊，今遭遇以疇祉。清切之地，愧非才賢之居；負秉之蕘，誓竭贊襄之力。直言國體，罔擇五術之工；殫究道眞，奚資七盛之詑？遠稽《十漸》，近取《五規》；法處厚《關雎》之陳，學孫奭《無逸》之解。倘進德愛身之疏，如可底行；庶責難陳善之恭，不爲虛語。伏願心純乾健，德懋晉昭。謨訓爲定保之徵，罔以側言而改度；紀綱敦愷悌之美，恒持宥密而執中。信順誕敷于九圍，瑤圖益固；文明光被于四表，寶曆彌昌。臣無任瞻天仰聖，激切屛營之至，謹奉
translation_en:
… [My study of] history followed the modest legacy of Jian [Sima Guang's] Shui [Luo commentary / Zizhi Tongjian, likely a transcription error for 涑水 Sushui] [?], yet I am barely able to observe the traces of success and failure; [my study of] the Classics came from the instruction of the school of the Cheng [brothers], yet in the end I have not fathomed the essence of the worthies and sages. In the past I lived in retirement and kept my counsel to myself ("tied up the sack"); now I have met with opportunity and been granted blessings. In this pure and intimate position [close to the throne], I am ashamed that it is not occupied by a person of talent and worth; yet as a humble firewood-gatherer bearing a load, I swear to exhaust my strength in assisting the state. Speaking frankly on matters of the state's dignity, I do not choose the artfulness of the "five techniques" [of persuasion]; thoroughly investigating the truth of the Way, what need is there to rely on the boastfulness of the "seven flourishes"? Looking far back, I examine the "Ten Gradual Failings" (Shijian) [by Wei Zheng]; looking near, I draw upon the "Five Admonitions" (Wugui) [by Sima Guang]. I model myself on [Wei] Chuhou's exposition of the "Guanju" [ode], and emulate Sun Shi's explanation of the "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) [chapter of the Book of Documents]. If my memorials on advancing in virtue and cherishing Your person can indeed be carried into practice, then perhaps the reverence of urging difficult tasks upon the ruler and setting forth what is good will not be empty words.

I humbly pray that Your mind may be as pure and vigorous as Heaven (Qian), and Your virtue as grand and bright as the advancing sun (Jin). May the counsels and instructions [of the ancestors] serve as the token of stability and preservation, never altering the standard on account of biased words; may the laws and institutions foster the beauty of benevolence and harmony, ever maintaining quiet profundity and holding fast to the Mean. Thus trustworthiness and compliance will be broadly spread throughout the nine regions, and the precious realm will become ever more secure; civilizing culture will brilliantly cover the four quarters, and the imperial calendar [reign] will grow ever more prosperous. Your servant is overwhelmed to the utmost with gazing up at Heaven and looking up to Your Sacred Majesty in earnest trepidation, and respectfully presents…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
命彰信攸同永清弘其化矣語業爲帝王
之大業也詩書所稱迄今爲烈唐虞三代
尚矣由漢而下英君誼辟非不代作然率
崇炫飾之虛文蔑躬行之實覆建武表章
六經勸學興禮而內多慾則惑也甘露詔
講五經同異石渠而王霸無異則雜也永
平幸三雍升堂辨說執經問難於前而弘
度未優則隘也建初會諸儒白虎觀如石
渠而外戚專恣則弱也貞觀增學舍生員
撰定五經疏而風焉雜夷則慚也太平興
國詔史館日進御覽三卷而天倫有議則
譎也紹興置春秋解座右禁有日課而忘
讎金虜則忍也寶慶讀中庸序不釋手至
恨不與同時而黥配葉李則悖也何以庶
幾於隆古哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝掃胡元之陋納之綱常倫理之中
如提裘振領天下翕然知道之有在也至
其
punctuated: 命，彰信攸同，永清弘其化矣。語業，爲帝王之大業也。《詩》《書》所稱，迄今爲烈，唐、虞、三代尚矣。由漢而下，英君誼辟非不代作，然率崇炫飾之虛文，蔑躬行之實覆。建武表章六經，勸學興禮，而內多慾則惑也；甘露詔講《五經》同異石渠，而王霸無異則雜也；永平幸三雍，升堂辨說，執經問難於前，而弘度未優則隘也；建初會諸儒白虎觀如石渠，而外戚專恣則弱也；貞觀增學舍、生員，撰定《五經》疏，而風焉雜夷則慚也；太平興國詔史館日進《御覽》三卷，而天倫有議則譎也；紹興置《春秋解》座右，禁有日課，而忘讎金虜則忍也；寶慶讀《中庸序》不釋手，至恨不與同時，而黥配葉李則悖也。何以庶幾於隆古哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，掃胡元之陋，納之綱常倫理之中，如提裘振領，天下翕然知道之有在也。至其
translation_en: … mandate, manifesting trustworthiness to all alike, and through eternal peace broadening their transformative influence. Speaking of achievements, these were the grand achievements of emperors and kings. What is praised in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing) and the Classic of History (Shujing) remains illustrious to this day; Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties are indeed supreme! From the Han dynasty onward, it is not that heroic rulers and righteous sovereigns failed to arise in succession, yet they generally revered showy and ornamental empty letters while slighting the substantive practice [?] of personal conduct. The sovereign of the Jianwu era [Emperor Guangwu of Han] promoted the Six Classics, encouraged learning, and revived rituals, yet inwardly he had many desires—this was delusion. The sovereign of the Ganlu era [Emperor Xuan of Han] decreed discussions on the similarities and differences of the Five Classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion (Shiquge), yet made no distinction between the Way of the True King and that of the Hegemon—this was adulteration. The sovereign of the Yongping era [Emperor Ming of Han] visited the Three Ritual Halls (Sanyong), ascended the hall to debate and expound, with scholars holding the classics and posing difficult questions before him, yet his breadth of magnanimity was insufficient—this was narrowness. The sovereign of the Jianchu era [Emperor Zhang of Han] assembled the Confucian scholars at the White Tiger Hall (Baihuguan) just as at the Stone Canal Pavilion, yet the consort clans monopolized power arbitrarily—this was weakness. The sovereign of the Zhenguan era [Emperor Taizong of Tang] increased the number of school buildings and students and commissioned the commentaries to the Five Classics, yet his household customs were mixed with barbarian ways—this was shameful. The sovereign of the Taiping Xingguo era [Emperor Taizong of Song] ordered the Historiography Institute to present three scrolls of the Imperial Reader (Taiping Yulan) daily, yet incurred criticism regarding natural familial relations—this was deceitfulness. The sovereign of the Shaoxing era [Emperor Gaozong of Song] placed the Explanations of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu jie) beside his seat and kept a daily reading schedule in the palace, yet forgot his enmity toward the Jurchen Jin barbarians—this was callousness. The sovereign of the Baoqing era [Emperor Lizong of Song] read the Preface to the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong xu) without putting it down, even regretting that he had not lived in the same era as its author, yet he tattooed and exiled Ye Li—this was perversity. How could any of them come close to high antiquity? Vastly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), he swept away the vulgarities of the barbarian Yuan and brought the realm back within the bounds of the cardinal principles and human ethics; like lifting a fur robe by its collar, all under Heaven harmoniously knew where the Way resided. As for his…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
命揭大學衍義廡壁而
語宋濂曾魯之言則所以切磨化源者又何
詳至歟我
成祖文皇帝黜百家之雜統以四書五經之正
如揭日行天天下曉然知學之有歸也至
其衍爲聖學心法一書而味人心虛靜之
旨則所以翼勵聖功者又何嚴密歟執事
謂宏綱庶政莫可殫述大要以務學爲本
信然矣是以
===
聖神謨烈上符唐虞遠邁三代而一時載筆之
臣莫能模擬其盛者
列聖繼承光昭前軌二百年來薄海內外沐仁
浸義修禮陳樂絃誦家聞詩書戶曉比屋
有可封之俗
享祚垂泰山之安猗歟休哉商周以還所未
有也至我
皇上茂齡纘序
光撫洪圖乃四禩于玆矣觀夫稽古右文類
punctuated: 命揭《大學衍義》廡壁，而語宋濂、曾魯之言，則所以切磨化源者，又何詳至歟！我成祖文皇帝黜百家之雜，統以《四書》《五經》之正，如揭日行天，天下曉然知學之有歸也。至其衍爲《聖學心法》一書，而味人心虛靜之旨，則所以翼勵聖功者，又何嚴密歟！執事謂宏綱庶政莫可殫述，大要以務學爲本，信然矣。是以聖神謨烈，上符唐虞，遠邁三代，而一時載筆之臣莫能模擬其盛者。列聖繼承，光昭前軌，二百年來，薄海內外沐仁浸義，修禮陳樂，絃誦家聞，詩書戶曉，比屋有可封之俗，享祚垂泰山之安。猗歟休哉！商、周以還，所未有也。至我皇上茂齡纘序，光撫洪圖，乃四禩于玆矣。觀夫稽古右文，類
translation_en: …ordering the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) to be posted on the corridor walls, and his remarks recorded in speaking to Song Lian 宋濂 and Zeng Lu 曾魯—how thorough and utmost were the means by which he polished the source of moral transformation! Our Emperor Chengzu Wen (the Yongle Emperor) rejected the杂heterogeneity of the Hundred Schools and unified learning with the orthodoxy of the Four Books and Five Classics, like holding up the sun to course through the heavens, so that all under heaven clearly knew where learning should be directed. And when it came to his expounding the book Methods of the Mind in Sage Learning (Shengxue xinfa) and savoring the purport of the human mind's emptiness and tranquility—how rigorous and precise were the means by which he assisted and encouraged sage cultivation! Your Excellency states that the grand principles and myriad administrative affairs cannot be exhaustively recounted, yet in essence they take devotion to learning as their foundation; this is truly so. Therefore, their sagely and divine plans and achievements matched Tang Yao and Yu Shun above and far surpassed the Three Dynasties, such that the court historians who wielded the brush at the time were unable to fully capture their magnificence. Successive Emperors inherited the throne, gloriously illuminating the tracks of their predecessors. For two hundred years, within and beyond the four seas, all have been bathed in benevolence and steeped in righteousness; rites have been cultivated and music displayed; the sound of stringed instruments and chanting is heard in every family, and the Odes and Documents are known to every household. Row upon row of homes possess customs worthy of enfeoffment, and the imperial throne enjoys a stability as enduring as Mount Tai. Oh, how magnificent! Since the Shang and Zhou dynasties, there has never been the like of this. Coming to our reigning Emperor, he succeeded to the imperial line in his youthful prime and has gloriously governed the great realm for four years now. Observing how his investigating antiquity and esteeming culture have generally…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
舉於
臨御之後訪經筵之舊章修太學之縟典蓋眞
以
祖宗成憲當遵寒暑政事不少輟焉所謂飭彝
憲以舉弘規而外以脩其文是矣乃復躬
蹈實踐潛脩爲心得之懿奉
聖母之歡顏
嘉輔臣之圖鑑蓋眞以二帝三王爲師
起居號令罔不臧焉所謂廣疇咨以惇素履
而內以懋其實是矣內外兼資文實並茂
其視漢唐宋目爲故事文具而實德則病
相去何如也肆今
===
聖德隆盛與日躋升光天海隅盡拜
帝道之賜文治熈洽窮髮絕鄙且爲一家斯重
學之驗已豈直橋門觀聽誇燿於漢營騎
授經稱美有唐哉天下喁喁謂
祖宗帝王之世復見愚也拭目太平安能揄揚
其萬一乎而執事尤拳拳思爲
punctuated: 舉於臨御之後：訪經筵之舊章，修太學之縟典，蓋眞以祖宗成憲當遵，寒暑政事不少輟焉。所謂「飭彝憲以舉弘規，而外以脩其文」，是矣！乃復躬蹈實踐，潛脩爲心得之懿；奉聖母之歡顏，嘉輔臣之圖鑑，蓋眞以二帝三王爲師，起居號令罔不臧焉。所謂「廣疇咨以惇素履，而內以懋其實」，是矣！內外兼資，文實並茂，其視漢、唐、宋目爲故事、文具而實德則病，相去何如也！肆今聖德隆盛，與日躋升，光天海隅，盡拜帝道之賜；文治熈洽，窮髮絕鄙，且爲一家。斯重學之驗已，豈直橋門觀聽誇燿於漢、營騎授經稱美有唐哉！天下喁喁，謂祖宗帝王之世復見。愚也拭目太平，安能揄揚其萬一乎？而執事尤拳拳思爲
translation_en: …instituted upon his accession to the throne: he has inquired into the old regulations for the Classics Colloquia and revived the elaborate ceremonies of the National University, truly holding that the established statutes of the Imperial Ancestors must be followed, and never slackening in the slightest amidst winter cold, summer heat, or the affairs of state. This is indeed what is meant by "putting in order the constant statutes to carry out the grand plan, and outwardly cultivating its form"! Moreover, he personally treads the path of practical implementation, quietly cultivating himself to attain the excellence of inward comprehension; he attends to the joyful countenance of the Sacred Mother and commends the illustrated mirror of history presented by his assisting ministers, truly taking the Two Emperors and Three Kings as his teachers, so that in his daily deportment and commands there is nothing that is not good. This is indeed what is meant by "broadening inquiries and consultations to consolidate pure conduct, and inwardly exerting oneself in its substance"! Drawing upon both the inner and the outer, with both form and substance flourishing together—how vast is the distance between this and the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, where such matters were treated as mere routine and outward formalities while substantive virtue suffered! Thus today, His Majesty's sacred virtue is grand and flourishing, ascending ever higher with each passing day; beneath the bright sky to the farthest corners of the seas, all bow to receive the bounty of the Imperial Way. Cultural governance is resplendent and harmonious, and even the barren lands and remotest frontiers are united as one family. This is already the proven efficacy of valuing learning—how could it merely be compared to the spectacle of observers thronging the arched gates of the university boasted of in the Han, or the teaching of the Classics to camp cavalry praised in the Tang! All under Heaven look up in eager admiration, saying that the age of the Imperial Ancestors and the ancient sage-emperors and kings has appeared once again. Wiping my eyes to behold this era of Great Peace, how could a foolish person like myself extol even one ten-thousandth of it? Yet Your Excellency still earnestly seeks to provide…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
聖天子惜時之助則宋臣范祖禹在元祐中有
是言也今雖欲殫竭忠慮將何以加焉蓋
我
皇上聖質方茂純一未鑿正宜務學之時也請
得畢其說蓋有三焉一曰進德二曰脩業
三曰愛身夫乾之進德貴於及時幼而習
之爲功則易今未明求衣日出開講究聖
經之奥旨納格心之正論愚固仰窺
上心之無雜慮矣然
===
人主當防未萌之欲
聖學貴豫養正之功大禹論愼位惓惓于安止
幾康之言周公勸敬德懇懇于自貽哲命
之訓故秉清明在躬時以裕存養可勿餒
也少之與長也異觀少之時耳目明達佗
無玩好人惟少之爲異及其長也情竇日
開將責備之者至焉故南山嚴裝未行鑾
徹已早還言矣後苑遊獵方舉韓休已促
諫疏矣曷若完固於初而使狂戇之章不
punctuated: 聖天子惜時之助，則宋臣范祖禹在元祐中有是言也。今雖欲殫竭忠慮，將何以加焉？蓋我皇上聖質方茂，純一未鑿，正宜務學之時也。請得畢其說，蓋有三焉：一曰進德，二曰脩業，三曰愛身。夫《乾》之進德，貴於及時，幼而習之，爲功則易。今未明求衣，日出開講，究聖經之奥旨，納格心之正論，愚固仰窺上心之無雜慮矣。然人主當防未萌之欲，聖學貴豫養正之功。大禹論愼位，惓惓于安止幾康之言；周公勸敬德，懇懇于自貽哲命之訓。故秉清明在躬時，以裕存養，可勿餒也。少之與長也異觀。少之時耳目明達，佗無玩好，人惟少之爲異；及其長也，情竇日開，將責備之者至焉。故南山嚴裝未行，鑾徹已早還言矣；後苑遊獵方舉，韓休已促諫疏矣。曷若完固於初，而使狂戇之章不
translation_en:
… an aid to the Sage Son of Heaven in cherishing his time, the Song official Fan Zuyu 范祖禹 already spoke these words during the Yuanyou reign (1086–1094). Today, even if I wish to exhaust my loyal thoughts, what could I add to them? Indeed, our August Emperor's sage nature is just now flourishing, pure and unspoiled—it is precisely the time when he ought to devote himself to learning. Allow me to set forth his argument in full, which has three parts: the first is called advancing in virtue, the second is called cultivating one's enterprise, and the third is called cherishing one's person.

Now, as for advancing in virtue in the Qian 乾 hexagram, what is valued is doing so in good time; if one practices it in youth, the effort is easy. Today, calling for his robes before dawn and opening the lectures at sunrise, investigating the profound meanings of the sage classics and accepting upright discourses that rectify the mind—foolish as I am, I have certainly looked up and glimpsed that the Sovereign's mind is free of distracting thoughts. Yet a ruler of men ought to guard against desires before they sprout, and sage learning values the work of nurturing rectitude beforehand. When the Great Yu 大禹 discussed being cautious on the throne, he was earnestly devoted to the words of resting calmly in where one abides and attending to the subtle springs of peace; when the Duke of Zhou 周公 urged reverent virtue, he was sincerely intent on the instruction of bequeathing to oneself a wise mandate. Therefore, holding fast to the time when pure clarity resides in one's person so as to enrich preservation and nourishment, one need not falter.

Youth and maturity are viewed differently. In youth, the ears and eyes are clear and perceptive, and there are no other frivolous amusements; people marvel at a ruler simply because he is young. When he grows up, however, the channels of passion open day by day, and those who expect perfection of him will arrive. Thus, before the grand procession to the Southern Mountains had even set out, Luan Che 鑾徹 [for Zhang Shizhi 張釋之 or Yuan Ang 爰盎?] had already submitted words urging an early return; as soon as a hunting excursion in the rear park was launched, Han Xiu 韓休 had already hastened his remonstrance memorial. How could that compare to being whole and firm from the very beginning, so that rash and blunt memorials do not…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
而已矣子貢之言語冉有之政事顏子之
德行非其殊塗特以諸子各得聖人之一
體而顏子則全體具而未能化也是故必
立功立言而希圖不朽者是求道之粗也
未若默成于德而自有輝光之發越也以
訓詁窮經而寡要爲儒者是命儒之淺也
未若默識于心而自得聖道之藴奥也執
事謂宋有儒林傳又有道學傳夫儒豈能
離道而爲學哉亦以諸儒通經學古猶爲
===
纂要鈎玄之習而周程諸君子則深造乎
聖道之全云耳然竊有疑焉張栻呂祖謙
與朱熹當時竝以道學稱者張栻得與道
學傳而祖謙不與焉何哉蓋以講明義利
之辯與夫稽物訂事之博造詣自有淺深
之不同也陸九淵與朱熹同時屢爲鵝湖
會者學非事乎口耳而不稱道學焉又何
哉蓋以徒知尊德性之爲大不知道問學
之爲精學術自有異同之難掩也是宋之
punctuated: 而已矣。子貢之言語、冉有之政事、顏子之德行，非其殊塗，特以諸子各得聖人之一體，而顏子則全體具而未能化也。是故必立功立言而希圖不朽者，是求道之粗也，未若默成于德而自有輝光之發越也；以訓詁窮經而寡要爲儒者，是命儒之淺也，未若默識于心而自得聖道之藴奥也。執事謂宋有《儒林傳》，又有《道學傳》。夫儒豈能離道而爲學哉？亦以諸儒通經學古，猶爲纂要鈎玄之習，而周、程諸君子則深造乎聖道之全云耳。然竊有疑焉：張栻、呂祖謙與朱熹，當時竝以道學稱者，張栻得與《道學傳》，而祖謙不與焉，何哉？蓋以講明義利之辯，與夫稽物訂事之博，造詣自有淺深之不同也。陸九淵與朱熹同時，屢爲鵝湖會者，學非事乎口耳，而不稱道學焉，又何哉？蓋以徒知尊德性之爲大，不知道問學之爲精，學術自有異同之難掩也。是宋之
translation_en:
…and nothing more. The speech of Zigong 子貢, the statecraft of Ranyou 冉有, and the virtuous conduct of Master Yan 顏子 [Yan Hui] did not follow divergent paths; it is merely that the other disciples each attained a single aspect of the Sage, whereas Master Yan possessed the whole substance, though he was not yet able to transform completely with it. Therefore, those who insist on establishing meritorious deeds or establishing words in the hope of achieving immortality are pursuing the coarse aspects of the Way; this is not as good as silently perfecting oneself in virtue, from which a radiant splendor naturally shines forth. Those who call themselves Confucians by exhausting the Classics through philological exegesis while lacking the essentials are giving a shallow definition to Confucianism; this is not as good as silently comprehending within the mind and naturally attaining the profound depths of the Sage's Way.

Your Excellency notes that the Song history has both the Biographies of Confucian Scholars (Rulin zhuan) and the Biographies of Masters of the Learning of the Way (Daoxue zhuan). Now, how could a Confucian possibly separate himself from the Way in pursuing his learning? It is simply that while those various scholars mastered the Classics and studied antiquity, they still engaged in the habit of compiling essentials and searching out obscurities, whereas noble men like Zhou [Dunyi 周敦頤] and the Cheng [brothers, Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤] penetrated deeply into the entirety of the Sage's Way. Yet I privately have a doubt about this: Zhang Shi 張栻, Lü Zuqian 呂祖謙, and Zhu Xi 朱熹 were all equally renowned in their own time for the Learning of the Way; why is it that Zhang Shi was included in the Biographies of Masters of the Learning of the Way while Zuqian was not included? It is because clearly elucidating the distinction between righteousness and profit, as opposed to broadly investigating things and verifying affairs, naturally involve different degrees of depth and shallowness in attainment. Lu Jiuyuan 陸九淵 was a contemporary of Zhu Xi and repeatedly held the Goose Lake (Ehu 鵝湖) meetings with him; his learning was not a matter of mere rote repetition by mouth and ear, yet he was not designated under the Learning of the Way—why is that as well? It is because he merely knew the greatness of honoring the moral nature, without knowing the refinement of inquiring and learning; in scholarly method there were naturally differences and similarities that could hardly be concealed. Thus the Song…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
道學傳也卽夫子所謂君子儒也學者盍
可以異觀之哉執事謂我
朝有名臣錄又有理學名臣錄夫名臣者孰
非循理以自淑哉無亦以諸公立朝大節
猶在設施事爲之間而薛胡諸君子獨用
心于內修之實云耳然亦有疑焉旣錄之
理學後學之仰止在是矣顧均名醇學之
儒名臣有或錄或否之異則昭示一定之
公論使人知所嚮往者不容已也理學編
===
次斯道之折衷有歸矣顧有屢請從祀於
孔廟而未有執筆以續之理學則明揭道
脉之誰屬使人知所準裁者不可後也是
我
朝之理學也卽宋之道學傳也學者可不知
所尚論哉嗚呼斯道之不明也皆起於似
是之亂眞空言性命爲元者其究窒於亨
之用詭遇事功爲利者其究賊於貞之體
吾儒之全體大用不如是也故體用會合
punctuated: 道學傳》也，卽夫子所謂君子儒也，學者盍可以異觀之哉？執事謂我朝有《名臣錄》，又有《理學名臣錄》。夫名臣者，孰非循理以自淑哉？無亦以諸公立朝大節，猶在設施事爲之間，而薛、胡諸君子，獨用心于內修之實云耳。然亦有疑焉：旣錄之《理學》，後學之仰止在是矣；顧均名醇學之儒，名臣有或錄或否之異，則昭示一定之公論，使人知所嚮往者，不容已也。《理學》編次，斯道之折衷有歸矣；顧有屢請從祀於孔廟，而未有執筆以續之《理學》，則明揭道脉之誰屬，使人知所準裁者，不可後也。是我朝之《理學》也，卽宋之《道學傳》也，學者可不知所尚論哉？嗚呼！斯道之不明也，皆起於似是之亂眞。空言性命爲元者，其究窒於亨之用；詭遇事功爲利者，其究賊於貞之體。吾儒之全體大用，不如是也。故體用會合，
translation_en:
… "Biographies of the Learning of the Way" (Daoxue zhuan), which are precisely what the Master called the "gentlemanly Confucian" (junzi ru). How could scholars view them differently?

You, sir, note that our Dynasty has the Record of Eminent Ministers (Mingchen lu) and also the Record of Eminent Ministers of the Learning of Principle (Lixue mingchen lu). Now, among eminent ministers, who did not follow principle to cultivate himself? Yet is this distinction not simply because the great integrity of those gentlemen at court was manifested in their policy measures and practical deeds, whereas masters like Xue [Xuan 薛瑄] and Hu [Juren 胡居仁] devoted their minds solely to the substance of inner cultivation? Even so, there is room for doubt here as well. Once they are recorded under the "Learning of Principle," later scholars look up to them as models; yet among Confucians equally renowned for pure learning, some are included among the eminent ministers and some are not. Thus, clearly setting forth a definitive public consensus so that people know toward what they should aspire is something that cannot be helped. With the compilation of the Learning of Principle, the balanced judgment of this Way has found its standard; yet there are those for whom canonization in the Temple of Confucius has been repeatedly requested, while no one has taken up the brush to continue recording them in the Learning of Principle. Thus, clearly holding up to whom the lineage of the Way belongs so that people know by what standard to judge is something that cannot be delayed. This Learning of Principle of our Dynasty is precisely the "Biographies of the Learning of the Way" of the Song; how could scholars not know how to evaluate them historically?

Alas! The obscuring of this Way always arises from the specious confounding the true. Those who engage in empty talk of human nature and destiny as "origination" (yuan) end up obstructed in the function of "flourishing" (heng); those who opportunistically pursue practical achievements as "advantage" (li) end up harming the substance of "correctness" (zhen). The complete substance and great functioning of us Confucians are not like this. Therefore, only when substance and function are united…

title: 萬曆四年貴州鄉試錄
text:
而盡性始有全功矣學術之不一也皆起
於黨同而伐異攻支離者廣大高明之量
以塞宗禪解者精微中庸之體以荒吾儒
之裕内豫外不如是也故内外一致而吾
心始無遺理矣嘗因是而論之宋儒以道
學名者學皆純于心性者也故張栻謂濂
溪之學淵源精粹寔自得於其心太極之
圖洞察主靜之爲本眞接洙泗之正傳矣
邢恕謂明道氣貌清明夷粹接人和而有
===
容其思索妙造精義其言近而測之益遠
誠爲成德之完人矣陳淳謂晦菴心度澄
朗瑩無查滓工夫縝密渾無隙漏孔孟周
程之道至先生而益明誠會其大而貫其
精矣此三儒者根心生色之妙百世之下
猶聞風而興也我
朝以理學名者功皆密於存養者也故薛瑄
之學以復性爲主浩然自得威勢不怵其
心去就不違其義觀于不言而躬行不露
punctuated: 而盡性始有全功矣。學術之不一也，皆起於黨同而伐異。攻支離者，廣大高明之量以塞；宗禪解者，精微中庸之體以荒。吾儒之裕内豫外不如是也，故内外一致，而吾心始無遺理矣。嘗因是而論之：宋儒以道學名者，學皆純于心性者也。故張栻謂濂溪之學，淵源精粹，寔自得於其心，《太極》之圖，洞察主靜之爲本，眞接洙泗之正傳矣；邢恕謂明道氣貌清明夷粹，接人和而有容，其思索妙造精義，其言近而測之益遠，誠爲成德之完人矣；陳淳謂晦菴心度澄朗，瑩無查滓，工夫縝密，渾無隙漏，孔、孟、周、程之道至先生而益明，誠會其大而貫其精矣。此三儒者，根心生色之妙，百世之下，猶聞風而興也。我朝以理學名者，功皆密於存養者也。故薛瑄之學，以復性爲主，浩然自得，威勢不怵其心，去就不違其義，觀于不言而躬行，不露
translation_en:
… only then does the fulfillment of one's nature achieve complete efficacy. The disunity of scholarly learning always arises from siding with those who agree and attacking those who differ. Among those who devote themselves to fragmented details, the capacity for breadth and lofty clarity becomes obstructed; among those who follow Chan Buddhist interpretations, the substance of subtle refinement and the Mean is laid waste. Our Confucian way of enriching the interior and preparing for the exterior is not like this; therefore, when interior and exterior are unified, our mind-and-heart finally leaves no principle uncomprehended.

I have previously discussed the matter on this basis: The Song Confucians who were renowned for the Learning of the Way (Daoxue) were all pure in their learning regarding the mind-and-heart and human nature. Thus, Zhang Shi 張栻 said that the learning of Lianxi 濂溪 (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤) was profound in its origins and pure in its essence, truly attained within his own mind-and-heart, and that his Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu) penetrated the fundamental principle of making tranquility primary, truly continuing the orthodox transmission of the Zhu and Si rivers (i.e., Confucius). Xing Shu 邢恕 said that Mingdao's 明道 (Cheng Hao 程顥)vitality and demeanor were clear, bright, tranquil, and pure; in dealing with others he was harmonious and tolerant; his reflections wondrously reached the finest subtleties of meaning, and his words, though near at hand, proved ever more profound the further one plumbed them—truly he was a consummate man of accomplished virtue. Chen Chun 陳淳 said that Huian's 晦菴 (Zhu Xi 朱熹) mind and measure were limpid and bright, crystalline without a speck of dross, and his effort of self-cultivation was fine and close-knit, wholly without gap or flaw; the Way of Confucius, Mencius, Zhou Dunyi, and the Cheng brothers became even clearer with the Master, who truly synthesized its greatness and threaded through its finest essentials. The wondrous quality of these three Confucians—rooted in the mind-and-heart and manifesting in their countenance—is such that even a hundred generations later, people are still inspired upon hearing of their character.

Those in our dynasty who are renowned for the Learning of Principle (Lixue) have all been meticulous in their efforts at preservation and nourishment. Thus, the learning of Xue Xuan 薛瑄 took the recovery of human nature as its main principle. Vastly self-possessed, coercion and power could not intimidate his mind-and-heart, and in accepting or leaving office he never violated righteousness.
